title: Political Strategies of India's Freedom Struggle

scenes.text: How did unarmed Indians defeat the British Empire without fighting an all-out war?
scenes.narration: Imagine trying to move a giant boulder using only your bare hands. India's freedom fighters faced the exact same puzzle against British rule, changing their strategy step by step.

scenes.text: Like a cricket test match, winning required patience, partnerships, and picking the right moment.
scenes.narration: Think of this as an analogy of a five-day cricket test match. You cannot hit every single ball for six; you defend patiently, build partnerships, and attack when the bowler gets tired.

scenes.heading: Moderates Versus Extremists

columns.title: Moderates
items: Constitutional dialogue, petitions, and assembly resolutions
Viewed British rule as just and beneficial

columns.title: Extremists
items: Direct mass action and public boycotts
Asserted self-rule as an immediate birthright

scenes.narration: Early leaders like Gokhale preferred polite petitions, believing British institutions brought justice. But Tilak and the extremists rejected slow appeals, demanding self-rule immediately as a birthright through public boycotts.

scenes.heading: Gandhian Struggle Cycle
scenes.narration: Here is the clever trick Gandhi understood: ordinary people cannot protest forever without getting exhausted. So, he alternated intense active struggles with peaceful truce periods dedicated to social unity and village constructive work.

scenes.heading: Major Mass Movements

events.what: Civil Disobedience Movement defying salt laws
Quit India Movement launching militant struggle

scenes.narration: The struggle grew in three powerful waves. Non-Cooperation tested national boycotts in 1920, Civil Disobedience challenged unjust salt laws in 1930, and Quit India launched an uncompromising mass uprising in 1942.

scenes.name: Bipin Chandra
scenes.idea: Characterized the freedom struggle as a unique, protracted, controlled mass movement.
scenes.narration: Historian Bipin Chandra observed that India's national movement succeeded because it was a protracted, controlled fight, carefully pacing mass pressure until colonial rule completely lost legitimacy.

items: Moderates built critique while extremists mobilized direct action.
Gandhi alternated mass struggle with constructive truce phases.
Successive movements escalated pressure until British departure.
scenes.narration: To remember this journey, picture three steps: moderates built the logical critique, Gandhi paced national energy through cycles of rest and action, and mass movements steadily forced the final British exit.
